3. In the course of execution of the said contract dispute arose between the parties as a result of which the opposite party instituted an Arbitration case on 9.6.1993 claiming a sum of US$7, 421, 234.50 and Tk. 121,958,483.00 under the various heads of claim which has been contested by the petitioner before the Arbitral Tribunal. It appears that during the course of Arbitral proceeding, the Arbitral Tribunal admitted into evidence certain documents and oral evidence of Mr. J. R. Clark allegedly illegally whereupon the petitioner has raised objection which was over-ruled by the Arbitral Tribunal. It further appears that the petitioner made a request for cross examining said Mr. Clark, a witness of the opposite party, but without giving a chance of cross-examination to the petitioner, his written statement was admitted into evidence by the Tribunal whereupon the petitioner was compelled to file Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997 before the First Court of subordinate Judge, Dhaka, under section 5 and section 41 of the Arbitration Act, 1940 and ultimately the Court by its judgment and order dated 5.4.2000 allowed the Arbitration Miscellaneous case and revoked the authority of the Arbitral Tribunal to proceed with the Arbitration case then pending before them. It further appears that in the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997, the petitioner prayed for temporary and ad-interim injunction to restrain the opposite party from proceeding with the ICC Arbitration Case No. 7934/CK/AER/ACS/MS but the Trial Court refused the prayer of ad-interim injunction by its order dated 16.11.1997 against which the petitioner preferred First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 252 of 1997 before the High Court Division. The High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 2.5.1999 allowed the appeal and also issued an order of injunction restraining the opposite party from proceeding with the said Arbitration Case and the said Judgment and order dated 2.5.1999 is annexed with the application and marked as Annexure-"B" to the application. It further appears that the opposite party filed a leave petition (C.P.S.L.A. No.622/ 1999) against the said judgment and order dated 2.5.1999 of the High Court Division but the Appellate Division refused leave and by judgment dated 22.7.1999 disposed of the petition without disturbing the order of temporary injunction. Thereafter the learned Sub-ordinate Judge after hearing both the parties allowed Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997 by his judgment dated 5.4.2000, which is evidenced by Annexure —"D" to the application. It appears that the learned Subordinate Judge by the aforesaid judgment allowed the said Miscellaneous Case on contest against the opposite party and revoked the authority of the Arbitral Tribunal to proceed with the ICC case No. 7934/ CK/AER/ACS/MS. It appears that inspite of repeated requests made by the petitioner and inspite of the Learned Subordinate Judge revoking the authority of the Arbitral Tribunal, the tribunal proceeded with the said ICC Arbitration Case and ultimately have given Award which is annexed as annexure "A" to the application and this case is filed to set aside the said Award passed by the Arbitral Tribunal in Arbitration Case No. 7934/ CK/ AER/ACS/MS dated 9.5.2003. 

 4. Mr. Salahuddin Ahmed, the learned advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the impugned award is a nullity in the eye of law being opposed to and in conflict with the law in force in Bangladesh and the public policy of Bangladesh inasmuch as the Award was made on 7.5.2003 long after the authority of the Tribunal had been revoked by the competent Court of law of this country namely the Learned Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous case No. 49/1997 by his judgment and order dated 5.4.2002. The learned advocate further submits that the said award is also opposed to and in conflict with the law in force in Bangladesh and the public policy of Bangladesh inasmuch as the award was made in disregard and violation of the judgment and order of the High Court Division dated 2.5.1999 passed in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 252 of 1997 as well as the High Court Division's order dated 27.5.2001 and 15.7.2002 made in Civil Revision No. 2736 of 2002. The learned advocate then submits that the Award is also not maintainable in law inasmuch as no opportunity was given to the petitioner to present its case and the petitioner was denied a written transcript of the proceeding despite its repeated requests. The learned advocate further submits that the Tribunal also misconducted the proceeding and also misconduct themselves by admitting inadmissible evidence and committed gross procedural impropriety thereby. The learned advocate further submits that the Tribunal also appeared to have abused its discretion and committed gross illegality and propriety in giving the Award against the petitioner without directing the opposite party to provide the information regarding insurance and ignoring the effect of such insurance payments in calculating the amounts under the Award. 

 5. In this case the opposite party did not enter appearance by filing any power nor appeared before this court at the time of hearing though notice was served upon the respondent through registered post with A/D dated 21.8.2003. Petitioner also served this notice through DHL on 20.8.2003. All the original registration slips dated 21.8.2003 and 20.8.2003 have been filed before this court as annexure "X", "X-1" with the affidavit of compliance filed by the petitioner on 24.8.2003. 

 7. On a perusal of the application and the papers annexed with the application it appears that this matter can be disposed of within a very short compass inasmuch as the admitted position is that the First Subordinate Judge in Arbitration Miscellaneous case No. 49/ 1997 by its judgment and order dated 5.4.2000 revoked the authority of the Arbitral Tribunal to proceed with any arbitration proceeding. It appears that the opposite party appeared and contested the said Miscellaneous Arbitration case but against the judgment of the Subordinate Judge did not prefer by appeal before the High Court Division. Therefore, the judgment dated 5.4.2000 passed in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49/1997 became final and parties to the contract are bound by it. It further appears that during pendency of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case a prayer for temporary injunction and ad-interim injunction was refused by the Subordinate Judge and against that order. First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 252 of 1997 was preferred by the petitioner. At the time of admission of the said Miscellaneous Appeal, the High Court Division passed an order of ad interim in-junction and that order was challenged by the opposite party No. 1 before the Appellate Division by Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 622 of 1999 but the Appellate Division vide judgment and order dated 22.7.1999 up held the order of injunction passed by the High Court Division after summarily rejecting the leave petition. Therefore, it also appears that there was injunction upon the Arbitral Tribunal not to proceed with the Arbitration proceeding during the pendency of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997. It further appears that ultimately the High Court Division by its Judgment and Order dated 2.5.1999 allowed the said First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 252 of 1997. 

 8. It further appears that against the order dated 30.4.2001 passed by the Arbitral Tribunal, the petitioner filed Title Suit No.189 of 2001 for the declaration that the purported procedural order dated 30.4.2001 was not binding upon the petitioner and that suit is still pending before the lower Court. It appears to me that by the judgment and order dated 5.4.2000 passed in Arbitration Misc. Case No. 49 of 1997 the authority of Arbitral Tribunal had been revoked on 5.4.2000. Thus the instant Title Suit No. 189 of 2001 which is now pending before the First Subordinate Judge, Dhaka has become infructuous. 

 9. In this case the substantive prayer of the petitioner is for setting aside the Award dated 9.5.2003 passed by the Arbitral Tribunal in Arbitration case No. 7934/CK/ AER/ ACS/MS. On a perusal of materials on record and particularly Annexure-"D" that is the judgment passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, First Court, in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997, it appears that the authority of the Arbitral Tribunal to proceed with the Arbitration Case No. 7934/CK/AER/ ACS/MS had been revoked on 5.4.2000. Therefore, the Arbitral Tribunal proceeded with the said arbitration case most illegally and without jurisdiction after the pronouncement of the judgment of Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997. Moreover, the Arbitral Tribunal was injuncted upon by the High Court Division not to proceed with the said arbitration case any further but in spite of that the Tribunal proceeded with the Arbitration Case and ultimately declared their Award on 9.5.2003. The admitted position is that the petitioner entered into a contract with the opposite party being agreement No. PIU/INF/ 1352 dated 14.2.1990 for installation of a pipeline of about 205 Kilometers under the second Gas Development Project of the Government of Bangladesh. Clause 1.1.38 of the Agreement provided for arbitration under the Rules of Conciliation and Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce and it also provided that venue of arbitration shall be Dhaka, Bangladesh. The applicable law of the agreement was set out in clause 1.1.1a. of the agreement in the following terms: 

 10. Thus it is clear that the Bangladesh Court has the jurisdiction to entertain a suit/proceeding if initiated by a party to the contract. Therefore the judgment passed by the First Subordinate Judge in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 49 of 1997 and the injunction order dated 2.5.1999 passed by this Court in First Miscellaneous Appeal No. 25 of 1997 were binding upon the Arbitral Tribunal but they ignored this aspect of the case and in flagrant violation of law of Bangladesh which govern the contract proceeded with the Arbitration proceeding. It is, thus, clear and obvious that the Award dated 9.5.2002 passed by the Arbitral Tribunal in Arbitration Case No. 7934/CK/AER/ACS/MS is a nullity in the eye of law and this Award can not be treated as an Award in the eye of law as it is clearly illegal and without jurisdiction inasmuch as the authority of the Tribunal was revoked as back as on 5.4.2000 by a competent Court of Bangladesh. Therefore, the impugned Award is no Award in the eye of law and it is a nullity in its entirety as it has no sanction of law. The so called Award is nothing but void abinitio and as such non est. Therefore, it appears to me from the facts and circumstances of the case that there is no scope to set aside the Award in question inasmuch as the Award is a nullity in the eye of law and has no legal existence at all. Therefore, it appears to me that the instant application is misconceived and incompetent. There is no necessity at all to set aside the Award, which is a nullity in the law and has no existence of its own as it is found that the impugned Award is a nullity in the eye of law. Therefore, the petitioner is not under any legal obligation whatsoever to comply with the direction given by the Tribunal in the impugned Award, which is non-est. Mr. Ahmed made a lengthy argument on merits of the case. He most emphatically urged before me that in any view of the matter I should enter into the merits of the case. True it is that there are sufficient materials on record to show that the Award suffers from patent illegality as it is mostly based on illegal and inadmissible evidence. Moreover, it is abundantly clear from the materials on record that the arbitrations misconducted themselves and misconducted the proceeding. Therefore, it can be said that the Award is not sustainable in law. But I need not advert to this aspect of the case in view of the fact that the Award is not an Award in the eye of law and thus it is non est. A non-existent award can neither be set aside nor can it be enforced. In that view of the matter it appears to me that the instant application is misconceived and thus incompetent in law. 

 11. In the result, the application is rejected, as it is misconceived and incompetent inasmuch as, there is no Award in the eye of law, which can be set aside by this Court.
